title: Rochdale Council Faces £15m Budget Deficit by 2029
excerpt: Rochdale Council could face a £15m budget deficit by 2029 if no action is taken, according to the latest financial forecast presented at a town hall meeting.
content_html:
Rochdale Council is projected to face a budget deficit of £15.227 million by the financial year 2029/30 if no measures are implemented. The latest budget forecast, presented to council leaders, highlights that rising wage costs, inflation, and increased pressures in adult social care and children’s services are contributing factors to this financial shortfall.

The finance team has expressed uncertainty regarding future government funding settlements, which complicates budget planning. Budget documents indicate a risk that the finance settlement for 2029/30 may not include a continuation of the Recovery Grant, which is currently around £15 million and only confirmed up to 2028/29.

In adult social care, the 'real living wage' continues to rise beyond expected levels, further straining budgets. An additional allocation of £1.5 million per year has been incorporated into future costs to address these pressures. Overspending in children’s services has also exceeded initial forecasts, a trend noted in recent years, according to finance officer Sam Smith.

During the town hall meeting on July 28, Councillor Daniel Meredith stated that significant efforts are underway to develop new care homes and children’s homes, expressing optimism about addressing the challenges in these services. The council has made savings of £204.5 million from its revenue budget since 2010/11, but the projected gaps mean that savings of £6 million will be required by 2028/29, escalating to £15 million by 2029/30.

title: Rochdale Local Plan Advances with Focus on Housing and Transport
excerpt: The Rochdale Local Plan aims to shape the borough's development until 2039, focusing on nearly 11,000 new homes and improvements to transport hubs.
content_html:
A new strategy to shape Rochdale's future has moved closer to implementation as the borough's Local Plan is set to undergo public consultation. The plan outlines how Rochdale will develop until 2039, with a focus on building nearly 11,000 new homes and transforming local transport hubs.

The Local Plan, which has been refined into a 175-page document, was approved by council leaders and is expected to be formally adopted in 2027. Initially, the plan required 20 per cent of new housing developments to be affordable, but this threshold has been adjusted to 15 per cent due to financial viability concerns. Councillor Daniel Meredith stated that this change does not reflect a reduced commitment to affordable housing, highlighting that the council has delivered 883 affordable homes in the past five years, exceeding previous targets.

Housing is a significant component of the Local Plan, with designated land for new developments already identified through the Places for Everyone strategy, which aims to create around 175,000 homes across Greater Manchester over the next two decades. The plan is expected to stimulate investment and redevelopment in Rochdale, particularly through the Atom Valley scheme, which aims to create 7,000 new homes and 20,000 jobs.

The Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy is central to the Local Plan, proposing the reconfiguration of land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This initiative aims to create vibrant spaces for living, working, and recreation, focusing on stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a new Slattocks station. The plan also includes improvements to walking and cycling routes, park and ride facilities, and community spaces, all intended to enhance the local economy.

title: Severely Neglected Toddler Rushed to Hospital After Social Services Case Closed
excerpt: A 19-month-old girl was admitted to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, revealing severe neglect and malnutrition.
content_html:
A 19-month-old girl, referred to as Child K1, was rushed to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, according to a recent Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale. The review reported that the toddler was found to be severely emaciated, weighing just 9.7lb (4.4kg), less than half the expected weight for her age, and covered in sores.

The review detailed that the child was severely dehydrated and had no fatty tissue on her body when she was admitted to critical care in February 2025. Medical professionals noted that she displayed "paper-thin skin" and had open pressure sores extending along her back, hips, and bottom. The case was closed despite warnings about a mother's neglect, who was only 17 when the child was born.

The review, conducted by expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall, highlighted that the toddler's mother had struggled with mental health issues and had avoided contact with social workers and health visitors. Following an anonymous tip in December 2024, social workers visited the home and confirmed the child's poor condition but were unable to secure consent for further intervention from the mother, leading to the case being closed due to insufficient evidence of significant harm.

Nineteen days after the case closure, the child was admitted to hospital, where medical staff noted a range of complications that could have led to death if not treated promptly. The findings of the review have prompted Rochdale Borough's Safeguarding Children Partnership to accept the conclusions and take action to address the issues identified.

title: Man jailed for taking weapons to Heywood school
excerpt: A man has been sentenced to two years in prison after taking a hammer, hatchet and kitchen knife to a school in Heywood, claiming he wanted to create a scene for attention.
content_html:
A man has been sentenced to two years in prison after taking a hammer, a hatchet and a kitchen knife to a school in Heywood. Both Douk Deng, 21, a South Sudanese national, was jailed at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court for his actions on August 6 last year.

Deng became increasingly frustrated with immigration authorities, having applied for and been refused asylum on three occasions. He intended to create a scene for attention to aid his cause, the court heard.

He was arrested after workmen confronted him at Edgar Wood Academy, which was closed to pupils for the summer. A member of the public had alerted the authorities after seeing Deng behaving oddly in the street nearby, carrying a petrol can with a hammer tied to his belt.

Deng was observed walking a full circuit around the school, mumbling to himself, before builders on site called the police due to their concerns.

excerpt: A 19-month-old girl was rushed to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, revealing severe neglect and malnutrition.
content_html:
A 19-month-old girl was admitted to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, according to a Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale. The toddler, referred to as Child K1, was found to be severely malnourished, weighing just 9.7lb (4.4kg), less than half the expected weight for her age.

The review revealed that the child was covered in sores and had no fatty tissue on her body. Medical staff noted her skin was "paper-thin" and that she displayed signs of severe dehydration. The case was closed despite concerns raised about a mother’s ability to care for her, as she had reportedly avoided contact with social workers and health visitors for weeks.

The review, conducted by expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall, highlighted that the child's grandmother had taken her to the hospital after she refused to eat. During this visit, family members informed hospital staff that the child was being neglected. Following this, the case was referred to Rochdale's Children's Social Care team, which initially assessed the mother as willing to accept support.

However, after an anonymous tip-off in December 2024 alleging severe neglect, social workers visited the home but were unable to secure the mother's consent for further intervention. A multi-agency strategy meeting concluded that the threshold for further action had not been met, leading to the case being closed. Nineteen days later, the child was admitted to critical care, suffering from multiple complications that could have been life-threatening without timely medical intervention.

title: Three men sentenced for running Rochdale's 'Adam Line' drug operation
excerpt: Three men have been sentenced for their roles in a Rochdale drug line that generated over £1 million a year, despite previous police efforts to dismantle it.
content_html:
Three men have been sentenced for their involvement in a drug line in Rochdale known as the 'Adam Line', which reportedly generated over £1 million a year. The operation continued despite multiple police interventions aimed at shutting it down.

Haider Ali, 34, known as 'The Ghost', was identified as the controller of the drug line. He was arrested after police observed a suspected drug deal on Baron Street. Officers found £1,000 in cash and wraps of cocaine and heroin on him, along with 75 wraps of cocaine and 32 wraps of heroin in the vehicle he was in.

Alan Ronald Ohara, 47, referred to as 'Rocket Ronny', was the driver, while 17-year-old Shane Walsh acted as Ali's lieutenant, responsible for preparing drugs for sale. Evidence presented in court indicated that Walsh had been involved in drug dealing since he was 16, and had continued his activities even after being released on bail.

The court heard that messages on Ohara's phone suggested he was involved in the management of the operation and was considering starting his own drug line. The prosecution highlighted the exploitation of Walsh, who had faced personal challenges and was groomed into the drug culture. Prosecutor Craig MacGregor noted that the gang had previously engaged in serious criminal activities, including bribing witnesses and using violence.

He called for increased stop and searches and a greater police presence across the region, rather than just in the city centre.

In addition to crime, Eckersley aims to build more affordable homes throughout Greater Manchester, focusing on developing brownfield sites to protect green spaces. Eckersley's policies align closely with those of Labour candidate Bev Craig, particularly regarding affordable housing and support for boroughs outside the city centre. However, he believes Labour has failed to deliver for the region during their time in control of the mayoralty since 2015. title: Andy Burnham Calls for Deportation of Rochdale Grooming Gang Leader
excerpt: Andy Burnham has vowed to take action to deport Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following his release from prison after serving 14 years for multiple rapes and sexual offences.
content_html:
A man called Shabir Ahmed, the leader of a grooming gang in Rochdale, was released from prison earlier this month after serving 14 years for multiple rapes and sexual offences against young girls. Ahmed, who was born in Pakistan, was stripped of his British citizenship as part of his sentence and has since renounced his Pakistani citizenship, leaving him stateless.

In response to Ahmed's release, Andy Burnham, the MP for Makerfield, stated, "Like everyone, I want this vile criminal out of the country." He has urged the home and foreign secretaries to explore all options for deporting Ahmed, emphasising that victims must come first. Burnham's comments come as he prepares for his anticipated role as prime minister.

The current home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, has indicated she will seek to amend the Immigration Act 1971 to facilitate Ahmed's deportation. However, there are significant challenges ahead, as Pakistan has reportedly refused to accept him back, complicating the deportation process. The Pakistani government has previously stated that it would only accept the deportation of Ahmed if Britain extradited certain Pakistani dissidents, which has been deemed unacceptable.

Burnham's commitment to this issue may lead to diplomatic tensions, as Britain could consider applying pressure on Pakistan through measures such as cancelling visas or halting foreign aid. The situation remains fluid as discussions continue regarding the deportation of Ahmed and other members of his gang, Qari Abdul Rauf and Adil Khan, who were also released from prison and have renounced their Pakistani nationality.

title: Rochdale Veteran Seeks Justice Following Nuclear Tests
excerpt: John Morris, a Rochdale veteran exposed to nuclear tests in the 1950s, expresses renewed hope for justice following the appointment of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who supports an independent inquiry.
content_html:
A man from Rochdale who was exposed to nuclear tests in the 1950s has expressed renewed hope for justice following the appointment of Prime Minister Andy Burnham. John Morris, now 88, was sent to Christmas Island in the Pacific Ocean at the age of 18, where he witnessed a series of nuclear detonations conducted by the Ministry of Defence (MoD).

Morris is part of a group of veterans who have lodged a criminal complaint against the MoD, claiming they have been denied justice regarding the health issues they suffered as a result of the tests. Many veterans have reported serious medical problems and are calling for an independent inquiry into their treatment. Burnham has previously supported the veterans' cause, stating that there is clear evidence of misconduct in public office. He has indicated that he backs a judicial review into the matter, which has given Morris and others hope for a resolution after years of campaigning.

The MoD has stated that compensation is available through the War Pensions Scheme, but many veterans feel this is insufficient. Morris believes that with Burnham's support, there is a chance for a thorough investigation into their claims. He has said that the new Prime Minister has finally given him hope of getting justice, as he continues to advocate for the rights of veterans affected by the nuclear tests.

In 2025, when Burnham was mayor of Greater Manchester, he expressed his view that the investigation into the treatment of veterans could not wait any longer, especially following the 80th anniversary of VE Day. Morris and his fellow veterans are now looking to the new Prime Minister to take decisive action on their behalf.

title: Hopwood Triangle Traffic Trial to Continue Pending Township Vote
excerpt: Rochdale Council has confirmed that the Hopwood Triangle traffic calming trial will remain in place until a formal township vote is conducted to decide its future.
content_html:
A traffic calming trial around the Hopwood Triangle in Heywood will continue pending a formal vote by the Heywood Township, Rochdale Council has announced. The trial, which introduced several changes to local roads, has faced significant criticism from motorists and residents since its implementation.

The measures include the closure of Middleton Road at its junction with Manchester Road near St John's Church, aimed at preventing drivers from using the route as a shortcut. Additionally, Magdala Street has been made one way towards Manchester Road, and new parking restrictions for heavy goods vehicles, along with a 20mph speed limit, have been introduced on surrounding residential roads.

North Heywood councillor Bev Place expressed disappointment that the trial would not end as soon as she had hoped. She stated that highways officers informed her that a township meeting must first vote to formally conclude the trial. Councillor Place is working to arrange an extraordinary meeting, as the next scheduled meeting is not until 22nd September.

In response to the ongoing concerns, a Rochdale Council spokesperson indicated that there is no set date for the removal of the traffic restrictions and that they are in discussions with contractors regarding the situation. Residents are encouraged to submit their views to the council's highways team via email to ensure their opinions are formally considered.

title: Rochdale's Local Plan to Shape Future with Thousands of New Homes
excerpt: Rochdale's Local Plan aims to build nearly 11,000 new homes and enhance transport hubs by 2039, with a council meeting set to discuss the proposal on July 28.
content_html:
A council meeting is scheduled for July 28 to discuss the Rochdale Local Plan, which aims to shape the borough's future by 2039. The plan includes the construction of nearly 11,000 new homes and significant changes around transport hubs.

The Local Plan is part of a broader strategy called Places for Everyone, which has been adopted by nine out of ten Greater Manchester councils. This strategy envisions the development of around 175,000 homes across the city region over the next two decades, with Rochdale expected to see substantial investment and redevelopment.

Key features of the Local Plan include the Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy, which proposes reconfiguring land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This initiative aims to create spaces for living, working, and leisure, focusing on stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a new Slattocks station.

The plan also addresses various topics such as climate and energy, economic growth, housing, and sustainable transport. The town centre is identified as a principal focus for regeneration, with recent developments including the £20 million redevelopment of Rochdale Town Hall, which is expected to become a key tourist attraction. The Local Plan is set to be pushed through to the next phase before formal adoption following the council meeting.

title: Green Party Candidate Geraldine Coggins Unveils Vision for Greater Manchester Mayoral Election
excerpt: Geraldine Coggins, Green Party candidate for Mayor of Greater Manchester, has outlined her plans for affordable housing and transport improvements, including free bus travel for young people and an orbital bus service.
content_html:
A Green Party candidate has outlined her vision for the Greater Manchester mayoral election, pledging to deliver 20,000 genuinely affordable homes and introduce free bus travel for young people if elected.

Geraldine Coggins, a councillor from Trafford, stated that her campaign focuses on taking Greater Manchester back from corporate interests. She plans to establish a programme called Homes for Greater Manchester, which aims to build 10,000 new homes and retrofit another 10,000, all offered at affordable rates. Coggins argued that this initiative would ultimately save taxpayer money by reducing reliance on temporary accommodation.

Coggins also proposed an orbital express bus service, named the B Orbit, which would connect towns across Greater Manchester, including Rochdale, Oldham, and Wigan. She emphasised the need for increased investment in areas outside Manchester city centre, which she believes has been neglected. Coggins described the free bus travel for those under 22 as a potential game changer for the region, promoting public transport as a normal and safe means of travel.

In addition to housing and transport, Coggins highlighted the importance of revitalising town centres and increasing funding for violence reduction initiatives. Her proposals include a £3 overnight visitor levy on hotel stays to support public transport improvements and the establishment of an empty shops team to help return vacant premises to use.
